elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor". The element is disjunctive and this contract has no Order Form structure (a single 36-month license), so agreement-level termination satisfies it.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor" — exactly 30 days, written, and no additional conditions or approvals attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "in which case Licensor shall refund pro rata any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination" — the words "pro rata" are express, not merely inferred from post-termination coverage.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Initial Period or any renewal term." The Initial Period is the defined 36-month committed term; retained Licensor termination rights (Article IV breach, Article XIX insolvency, Article XX wind-up) are all cause-based and do not contradict.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on thirty (30) days' notice, which is outside the stated 60–90 day fallback band (and is more favourable to us, consistent with the preferred level).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: no early-termination fee, penalty, or accelerated-payment mechanic is imposed on Licensee anywhere in the cited or inserted language, so the cap condition does not arise.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Satisfied a fortiori — Licensor is given no convenience right at all during the Initial Period or any renewal term, so it cannot terminate for convenience mid-term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: Licensor holds no convenience termination right under the amended text, so no notice period is required.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met in operative language (30 days' written notice, express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on Licensor convenience termination during the Initial Period or any renewal term).

Fallback is not independently complete because the notice period is 30 days rather than 60–90 days; that is immaterial since the preferred checklist is fully satisfied and the shorter notice favours Licensee.

Minimal: a single concise insertion for a genuinely missing clause. No existing words are deleted or paraphrased, the model-language surplus "in whole or in part" was correctly omitted (no Order Form or partial-termination structure exists), and no extras such as survival tails, procedures, or damages categories were added. "or any renewal term" is within the checklist's "committed term" scope, not an extra requirement.

Preserves intent: Licensor's cause-based termination rights (Article IV breach, Article XIX insolvency, Article XX wind-up/change of control) and the payment-retention sentence survive unchanged and do not contradict the new convenience right; the clause uses the defined term "Initial Period" and leaves no dangling cross-reference or undefined trigger.

Finding status "deviation" is correct: the 36-month Initial Period contained no Licensee exit right at all, which is walk-away territory under T4C; the RENEWAL point (Licensor's unilateral 7-year option) is properly left to its own rule rather than double-flagged here.
